program.section_heading: AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE, ASSOCIATE IN ARTS
outcomes: Engage in conversation and interactions with users of ASL employing the necessary rules of pronunciation, grammar, and syntax.
Understand and interpret ASL and respond to it at all levels of proficiency.
Understand and interpret texts (video) in ASL at various levels of proficiency.
Convey information, concepts, and ideas in text (video) of the target language to an audience on a variety of topics.
Exhibit a comprehensive understanding of Deaf culture and its social and cultural influences.

notes: The SIGN 2B row prints '5-6' and reads 'SIGN 2B or SIGN 10 & SIGN 20': the alternative is SIGN 10 and SIGN 20 taken together, not either one alone. Units 5 / units_max 6 reflect the printed row range; individual units for SIGN 10 and SIGN 20 are not printed on this page, so they are null.
'Additional Requirements 36-37' covers competency requirements, the GE pattern and electives together; it is not recorded as ge_units because it is not a GE-only figure.
Total Units 60 is printed as this award's total and is recorded as degree_total; electives fill the remainder 'if needed', with no units printed.

Careers are taken from the description: 'pursue a career or further degrees in ASL, Deaf Studies, interpreting, linguistics, education, audiology, and other related fields'. These fields are named for careers or further degrees together.
